intro: A letter series is a list of letters (or groups of letters) that follows a hidden rule. Turn the letters into numbers, find the rule, then fill in the missing term.

tips.title: Number the letters
tips.body: Write A = 1, B = 2 … Z = 26. Remember EJOTY: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25. Now a letter series is just a number series.

tips.title: Count the jumps
tips.body: Count how many letters you jump between neighbours. Equal jumps (+3, +3), growing jumps (+2, +3, +4) and jumps in pairs (+2, +2, +3, +3) are the most common.

tips.title: After Z comes A
tips.body: The alphabet goes round in a circle. Y + 6 is E: count on past Z, or work out 25 + 6 = 31 and take away 26.

tips.title: Groups? Split them into columns
tips.body: For groups like BY, GT, LO, look at the 1st letters on their own (B, G, L), then the 2nd letters (Y, T, O). Each column has its own rule.

tips.title: Back and forth? Two series
tips.body: If the letters jump back and forth, as in C, K, D, L, E, M, split them into odd places (C, D, E) and even places (K, L, M).

tips.title: Look for shuffled blocks
tips.body: Groups like EGF, HJI, KML use letters in a row (E F G) written in a fixed order. Find the order once, then use it on the next block.
